reset.impact: external handshakes can be observed at the synchronous reset edge even though the reset branch discards the transaction

logical_cache.scope: total logical capacity only under the implemented one-block-at-a-time invalidation lifetime
logical_cache.implementation: behavioral register-array cache with combinational selection

logical_reads.calculation: 4 selected sources * 96 lanes * 8 bits = 3072 bits per accepted update

p1.title: reset does not quiesce public valid/ready/accept handshakes
p1.evidence: independent VCS observes one fill accept, one row accept, one update valid and one update accept while rst_core is high
p1.required_action: gate ready/valid/accept with !rst_core, add reset-quiescence SVA, and define whether pre-reset pending work is aborted or drained

p2.title: 1536-byte cache and 3072-bit reads are logical, not a physical macro implementation
p2.required_action: bind a realizable multi-read/register-banked organization and run DC/STA/power before any physical performance claim

p2.title: M123 forwarding accumulator is not integrated
p2.required_action: build an exact-SHA wrapper miter covering consecutive same-row K4 updates through accumulator commit

p2.title: input valid is fail-closed rather than ordinary decoupled ready/valid
p2.evidence: any row_valid or weight_fill_valid asserted while its semantic-ready preconditions are false becomes a sticky protocol fault
p2.required_action: document the request contract or add non-faulting backpressure semantics before composition

safe_claim: Exact-SHA commercial VCS and an independent adversarial scoreboard validate reset-free M125 canonical lowest-four select-and-clear, source conservation, block-phased cache identity, stall stability, mixed polarity, and exact signed11 fold arithmetic including +512 and -512. The 1536-byte cache and 3072-bit reads are logical architecture quantities. The 3.1725x result remains an M122 fixed8 service-island cycle projection (1.2513x incremental over K1), not an M125 RTL-measured, physical, full-network, or system speedup.
